title: Allow People Choices When Instituting Change to Smooth the Transition
excerpt: Allow People Choices When Instituting Change to Smooth the Transition Via Lifehacker by Eric Ravenscraft Change is almost certain to upset people when it's forced on them. If you're in a position where you have to impose change on someone else, giving them some form of choice can help make the medicine easier to swallow. Whether you're a manager changing direction for your company or a parent that has to move your kids to a new home and school, change is always hard to pitch. As author Liz Keever explains, leaving some kind of option—even if the overall shift is still mandatory—can make people more willing to give your changes a chance. title: ​Quiet Slamming Doors With Felt Pads
excerpt: ​Quiet Slamming Doors With Felt Pads Via Lifehacker by Tori Reid The sound of a door slamming can be alarming, to say the least. Quiet them with some simple felt pads from your local home store. This trick from Home Hacks is a bit better concealed than the rubber band trick we've talked about before. Grab one or two felt pads and stick them inside the door frame. You can put them around the lock area, or spread them out closer to the top and bottom. The pads will catch the door before it hits the frame. While it won't completely silence the slam, it will quiet it, providing you some protection from the sound.
